intro.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that automatically refreshes an expired authentication token using Axios interceptors. You will learn how to intercept HTTP requests and responses to check for token expiration and handle a refresh request seamlessly. The core concepts involve using Axios interceptors, managing asynchronous API calls, and updating application state with the new token. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to maintain user sessions in a secure and efficient way within a React app.
intro.usecase: Token refresh with Axios interceptors is a foundational pattern for maintaining secure user sessions in modern web applications. You'll implement this in dashboards for SaaS platforms like project management tools or analytics services, where users remain logged in for extended periods without manual re-authentication. It's also critical in e-commerce checkouts, banking portals, and admin panels, ensuring uninterrupted access while silently refreshing expired tokens in the background. As a developer, you'll use this to handle 401 errors gracefully, providing a seamless experience instead of forcing users to repeatedly log in.
